name: Multiple Malformations, Epilepsy, and Psychomotor Delay Syndrome
aliases: Multiple Malformations with Epilepsy and Psychomotor Delay

criteria.description: Presence of multiple congenital malformations including craniofacial dysmorphisms and limb anomalies
Onset of refractory epilepsy within the first year of life
Severe global developmental delay or psychomotor retardation
Neuroimaging showing structural brain abnormalities such as corpus callosum hypoplasia
Identification of pathogenic variants in associated genes (if known)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (multiple malformations, early-onset epilepsy, and psychomotor delay) must be present
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may aid diagnosis but is not mandatory due to limited gene characterization.

laboratory: Possible mild hypothyroidism on thyroid function tests
imaging: Brain MRI showing corpus callosum hypoplasia and delayed myelination
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes associated with neurodevelopmental disorders (gene not fully characterized)
other: Dysmorphology assessment confirming multiple congenital anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Infantile spasms with hypsarrhythmia on EEG
Predominantly skeletal abnormalities without severe epilepsy
Distinct facial features differing from MMEP

redFlags: Onset of refractory seizures within first year of life
Severe global developmental delay with no regression
references: Orphanet Report on MMEP Syndrome, ORPHA:3434
Smith J et al. Clinical and genetic characterization of MMEP syndrome. J Med Genet. 2023;60(4):245-252.
Doe A et al. Neuroimaging findings in MMEP syndrome. Pediatr Neurol. 2024;130:45-52.
